definitions.title: Convergence of an Infinite Sequence
definitions.latex: \lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = L \iff \forall \epsilon > 0, \; \exists N \text{ s.t. } n > N \implies |a_n - L| < \epsilon
definitions.statement: A sequence {a_n} converges to limit L if its terms approach L arbitrarily closely as n increases without bound. If no finite limit exists, the sequence diverges.
definitions.explanation: Continuous limit theorems (Squeeze Theorem, L'Hopital's Rule applied to a(x)) carry over directly to discrete sequences.
definitions.keyTakeaway: A sequence is an ordered list of numbers whose convergence is governed by limits at infinity.

definitions.title: Monotone Convergence Theorem
definitions.latex: a_n \le a_{n+1} \quad \text{and} \quad a_n \le M \implies \lim_{n \to \infty} a_n \text{ exists}
definitions.statement: Every bounded, monotonic sequence of real numbers converges to a finite real limit.
definitions.explanation: Fundamental completeness property of the real numbers: bounded increasing sequences converge to their least upper bound (supremum).
